glosses: gerund of zertrampeln
to crush violently (especially underfoot), to trample
растоптать; раздавить (ногами)
deptać, tratować
Détruire en piétinant.

examples.text: Die Kinder haben im Garten getobt und dabei Omas schöne Blumen zertrampelt!
examples.translation: Les enfants se sont défoulés dans le jardin et ont piétiné les belles fleurs de grand-mère !

glosses: durch Schritte/Tritte (Trampeln) beschädigen oder zerstören

examples.text: „Sie warfen Tränengasgranaten und zertrampelten mit Ingrimm die Transparente, auf denen zu lesen stand: »Wir wollen keinen Kommunismus am Kongo! Fort mit dem Neokolonialismus Lumumbas! Lumumba, tritt zurück!«“
Geh bitte nicht über das Feld, du zertrampelst die jungen Pflänzchen.
Sie hatte Angst, von dem immer unruhiger werdenden Elefanten zertrampelt zu werden.

glosses: To crush something by walking on it.

examples.text:
Our conquering ſwords ſhal marſhal vs the way
UUe vſe to martch vpon the ſlaughtered foe:
Trampling their bowels with our horſes hoofes: […]
neither caſt ye your pearles before ſwine: leſt they trample them vnder their feete, […]

Everything a living animal could do to destroy and to desecrate bed and walls had been done. […] A canister of flour from the kitchen had been thrown at the looking-glass and lay like trampled snow over the remains of a decent blue suit with the lining ripped out which lay on top of the ruin of a plastic wardrobe.

glosses: To treat someone harshly.
To walk heavily and destructively.

examples.text:
June 9, 1960, Charles Dickens, All the Year Round
[…] horses proud of the crimson and yellow shaving-brushes on their heads, and of the sharp tingling bells upon their harness that chime far along the glaring white road along which they trample […]

glosses: To cause emotional injury as if by trampling.

examples.text: to trample on our Maker's laws

glosses: A heavy stepping.

examples.text: Newly harvested grapes are poured into a vast vat for everyone to have a good trample upon […]

glosses: The sound of heavy footsteps.
To trample heavily.

examples.text:
Everybody clap your hands
Get up and dance

Get up and feel the beat
We're gonna stomp all night now

glosses: To stamp (one’s foot or feet).
To severely beat someone physically or figuratively.
To completely defeat or overwhelm an enemy, to win by a large lead over someone
To crush grapes with one's feet to make wine
A deliberate heavy footfall; a stamp.

examples.text: She obliterated the cockroach with one stomp.

glosses: Any of various dances incorporating repeated heavy, rhythmic steps.

examples.text:
Well, let's dance, well let's dance.
We'll do the twist, the stomp, the mashed potato too
Any old dance that you want to do
But let's dance.

glosses: A style of jazz music for stomp dances of the early twentieth century.
A piece of music in this style.
A social gathering where dancing is the main activity; a dance.

examples.text: We’re going to a stomp tonight.
